question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

____ architect designed ____ modern office building and ____ traditional residential home, showcasing ____ blend of contemporary and classic architectural styles.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. An; a; a; a.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The choice of "a"/"an" depends on the sound of the following word:

◦ "architect" begins with a vowel sound (/ɑː/) → "An architect".

◦ "modern", "traditional" and "blend" all begin with consonant sounds → "a modern", "a traditional", "a blend".

◦ Correct: An architect designed a modern office building and a traditional residential home, showcasing a blend ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The other options wrongly use "an" before a consonant sound (an traditional/an blend), which is incorrect.

NOTE

• Rule: use "an" before a vowel sound (an architect, an hour, an MP) and "a" before a consonant sound (a modern, a university, a one-way street).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Fast
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Quick.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fast" means moving or done at high speed; rapid. Its closest synonym is "quick". (तेज़ / द्रुत)

◦ Example: He is a fast/quick runner.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Barely" (hardly) is unrelated.

• Option 3 "Tardy" (slow/late) and Option 4 "Languid" (slow, relaxed, lacking energy) are antonyms of fast.

NOTE

• Synonyms of fast: quick, rapid, swift, speedy, brisk.

• Antonyms: slow, sluggish, tardy, languid, leisurely.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The athlete's performance was __________, earning him a standing ovation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. exceptional.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "standing ovation" (the audience standing up to applaud) is given for an outstanding performance, so the blank needs a strongly positive word. "Exceptional" means unusually good or outstanding. (असाधारण / उत्कृष्ट)

◦ Correct: The athlete's performance was exceptional, earning him a standing ovation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "mediocre" (of poor/ordinary quality), 3 "moderate" and 4 "average" all suggest ordinary performance, which would not earn a standing ovation.

NOTE

• Synonyms of exceptional: outstanding, remarkable, extraordinary, superb, excellent.

• Antonyms: mediocre, ordinary, average, unremarkable.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word 'Flash' from the given sentence.

My cousin Zara, who loves to explore outer space in her free time, once noticed or observed a disc-shaped object blinking in the sky.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. blinking.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Flash" means to shine/light up briefly and repeatedly. Its synonym in the sentence is "blinking" (shining on and off). (चमकना / टिमटिमाना)

◦ Example: The lighthouse light kept flashing/blinking in the dark.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "noticed" and 2 "observed" mean "saw", and Option 3 "explore" (to investigate) do not mean "flash".

NOTE

• Synonyms of flash: blink, gleam, glint, sparkle, twinkle. "Flash" refers to a sudden, brief burst of light (a flash of lightning).

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

I cannot call him directly as I have lost his support.
option_1: am out of favour with him
option_3: am quite at sea with him
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. am out of favour with him.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to be out of favour (with someone)" means to have lost someone's approval, support or goodwill. It fits "I have lost his support". (किसी की कृपा/समर्थन खो देना)

◦ Example: After the argument, he was out of favour with his manager.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "at sea" (confused) and Option 4 "in character" (typical of someone) do not fit.

• Option 2 "in my own light" is not a standard idiom for losing support.

NOTE

• Opposite idiom: "in someone's good books / in favour with someone" (to have their approval). "Out of favour" = to have lost approval.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The Indian Government has launched the National Rural Livelihoods Mission, a _________ programme aimed at reducing rural poverty.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. flagship.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "flagship programme" means the most important, leading or prominent programme of an organisation/government. The National Rural Livelihoods Mission is described positively as a leading anti-poverty programme. (प्रमुख / अग्रणी कार्यक्रम)

◦ Correct: ... a flagship programme aimed at reducing rural poverty.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "controversial" (causing dispute), Option 2 "regressive" (becoming worse/backward) and Option 4 "designer" (relating to fashion) all carry a wrong/negative sense here.

NOTE

• "Flagship" originally means the lead ship of a fleet; figuratively, the best/most important product, scheme or programme (a flagship scheme, a flagship store).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.

Suman will be fired if she did not complete the delegated target set by her boss.
option_2: if she do not complete the delegated target
option_3: if she had not complete the delegated target
option_4: if she does not complete the delegated target
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. if she does not complete the delegated target.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This is a first conditional (real/likely future) sentence: "will + base verb" in the main clause requires the simple present in the "if" clause. As "she" is singular, it takes "does not complete".

◦ Correct: Suman will be fired if she does not complete the delegated target ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 keeps the wrong "did not" (past).

• Option 2 "do not" is wrong for the singular "she".

• Option 3 "had not complete" is grammatically incorrect.

NOTE

• First conditional: If + simple present, ... will + base verb. "If she does not finish, she will be fired." Use "does" with singular subjects (he/she/it).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

(1) Malini's family (2) doesn't know (3) how she bears out (4) the work pressure.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. how she bears out.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal verb to mean "to endure/tolerate" is "bear" (or "bear up under"), not "bear out" (which means to confirm/support a statement).

◦ Correct: Malini's family doesn't know how she bears the work pressure. (or "bears up under")

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Malini's family", "doesn't know" and "the work pressure" are all correct.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "bear": bear (with) = tolerate/endure; bear out = to confirm (the facts bore out his claim); bear up = to cope with difficulty. Here the sense is "endure", so "bears" (not "bears out").

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

His skills in programming / are more superior than / most developers / in the company.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. are more superior than.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "superior" is already a comparative (from Latin) and is followed by "to", not "than". Also, "more" should not be used with it. So it should be "superior to".

◦ Correct: His skills in programming are superior to most developers' (skills) in the company.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "His skills in programming", "most developers" and "in the company" are acceptable.

NOTE

• Latin comparatives take "to" (not "than") and never take "more": superior to, inferior to, senior to, junior to, prior to, preferable to.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A short stay at a place.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Sojourn.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "sojourn" is a short/temporary stay at a place. (अल्पकालिक प्रवास / कुछ समय का ठहराव)

◦ Example: During his sojourn in Paris, he visited many museums.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Xenophobe" — a person who fears/dislikes foreigners.

• Option 2 "Embargo" — an official ban on trade/activity.

• Option 3 "Topiary" — the art of trimming trees/shrubs into shapes.

NOTE

• Related travel/stay words: sojourn (short stay), itinerary (travel plan), expedition (a journey with a purpose), pilgrimage (a religious journey).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

A famous economist / says that / the government should do more / for create enough jobs.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. for create enough jobs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To express purpose, we use the to-infinitive ("to create"), not "for + base verb". So "for create" should be "to create".

◦ Correct: A famous economist says that the government should do more to create enough jobs.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "A famous economist", "says that" and "the government should do more" are all correct.

NOTE

• Infinitive of purpose = "to + base verb" (to create, to earn, to improve). "For + verb-ing" is used for the function of something (a knife for cutting), but purpose after a clause uses "to + verb".

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical/spelling error.

Jack along with / his family visited / his aunt living / at America.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. at America.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• With large areas such as countries and continents, we use the preposition "in", not "at". So it should be "in America".

◦ Correct: Jack, along with his family, visited his aunt living in America.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Jack along with", "his family visited" and "his aunt living" are all acceptable (note: "Jack along with his family" takes a singular verb — "visited" is fine as past tense).

NOTE

• Prepositions of place: "in" for large areas (in America, in India, in a city); "at" for specific points (at the bus stop, at the airport, at a small place).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Sycophant
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Fawner.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "sycophant" is a person who flatters powerful people to gain favour; a flatterer/toady. Its closest synonym is "fawner" (one who fawns/flatters excessively). (चापलूस / खुशामदी)

◦ Example: The king was surrounded by sycophants/fawners who praised his every word.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Arrogant" (haughty), Option 2 "Uppity" (self-important) and Option 4 "Independent" are not synonyms of sycophant.

NOTE

• Synonyms of sycophant: flatterer, fawner, toady, bootlicker, yes-man.

• To "fawn over" someone = to try to please them with excessive flattery.

question:
Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence and select its correct spelling from the given options.

The teacher assessed the student's flyer for writing.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. flair.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The intended word is "flair", meaning a natural talent or aptitude for something. The word "flyer" (a leaflet/pamphlet) is wrong in this context; the teacher assessed the student's flair (talent) for writing. (स्वाभाविक प्रतिभा / योग्यता)

◦ Correct: The teacher assessed the student's flair for writing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "flare" (a sudden burst of flame/light), Option 3 "fire" and Option 4 "friar" (a member of a religious order) do not fit the sense of natural talent.

NOTE

• Homophones: "flair" (natural talent) and "flare" (a burst of flame / to widen). "She has a flair for languages" vs "The candle flared up".

question:
Select the most appropriate option with the correct usage of the preposition to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) was born during 16 November 1945.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. was born on 16 November 1945.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• With specific dates, we use the preposition "on". So it should be "born on 16 November 1945". (तिथि के साथ 'on')

◦ Correct: UNESCO was born on 16 November 1945.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "by" (deadline), Option 3 "at" (specific time/point) and Option 4 "in" (months/years/longer periods) are wrong for a full date.

NOTE

• Prepositions of time: "on" for days and dates (on Monday, on 15 August); "in" for months/years/seasons (in 1945, in November); "at" for precise times (at 5 o'clock, at noon).

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence.

The restaurent's atmosphere was pleasant and inviting.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. restaurent's.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Restaurent" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Restaurant", meaning a place where meals are prepared and served to customers. (रेस्तराँ / भोजनालय)

◦ Correct: The restaurant's atmosphere was pleasant and inviting.

• Spelling key: RES + TAU + RANT — it ends in "-rant" (the word "rant"), borrowed from French.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "inviting", "atmosphere" and "pleasant" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• French-origin words with tricky spellings: restaurant, cuisine, buffet, gourmet, entrepreneur, questionnaire. Remember "restau-rant".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Vacant
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Empty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Vacant" means not occupied; empty or unfilled. Its closest synonym is "empty". (खाली / रिक्त)

◦ Example: There were several vacant/empty seats in the theatre.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Full" is an antonym of vacant.

• Option 2 "Brutal" (cruel) and Option 4 "Popular" (liked by many) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of vacant: empty, unoccupied, unfilled, void, free.

• Antonyms: full, occupied, filled, taken. (A "vacant look" also means a blank/expressionless look.)

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Mithya's remarkable generosity extended to everyone she knew.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Selfishness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Generosity" means the quality of being kind and willing to give/share freely. Its antonym is "selfishness", meaning caring only about oneself. (उदारता का विलोम — स्वार्थ)

◦ Example: Her generosity in helping the poor was the opposite of his selfishness.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Perfection", Option 2 "Cowardice" (lack of courage) and Option 3 "Awkwardness" (clumsiness) are unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of generosity: kindness, liberality, magnanimity, benevolence.

• Antonyms: selfishness, meanness, stinginess, miserliness.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Burn the midnight oil
option_3: To work late into the night
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To work late into the night.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to burn the midnight oil" means to work or study late into the night. (देर रात तक काम/पढ़ाई करना)

◦ Example: Before the exam, she burned the midnight oil to finish the syllabus.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 4 take the idiom literally or reverse its meaning.

NOTE

• The idiom dates from the time when people used oil lamps to work at night. Similar expressions: "work round the clock", "pull an all-nighter".

question:
Select the correct spelling from the given options to fill in the blank.

I hope you will excuse me for doing what is only my duty, although it may appear __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. impertinent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "impertinent", meaning rude, disrespectful or not showing proper respect. (धृष्ट / अशिष्ट)

◦ Example: It was impertinent of the boy to answer his teacher back.

• Spelling key: IM + PER + TI + NENT — ends in "-nent" (as in prominent, permanent).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "impertiant", 2 "impertaint" and 4 "impertinant" are all misspellings.

NOTE

• "Impertinent" = rude/insolent. Do not confuse with "pertinent" (relevant/to the point). Related: impertinence (noun), impertinently (adverb).

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

One day we saw Kala Nag. The monsoons had burst with all their fury, and it had rained in the night. The earth, which had lain parched and dry under the withering heat of the summer sun, was teaming _____1_____ life. In little pools, frogs croaked. The muddy ground was littered with ____2___ worms, centipedes and velvety lady-birds. Grass ____3____ begun to show and the banana leaves glistened bright and glossy green. The _____4___ had flooded Kala Nag's hole. He sat in an open patch on the lawn. His shiny black hood glistened in the sunlight. He was big, almost six feet in _____5____ and rounded and fleshy, as my wrist. "Looks like a King Cobra. Let's get him."

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. with.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The expression "teeming with (life)" means full of / abounding in. So the earth "was teeming with life" — full of living creatures after the rain. (से भरपूर)

◦ Correct: ... the earth ... was teeming with life.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "teeming before/in/at life" are not correct collocations.

NOTE

• "Teem with" = to be full of / swarm with (a pond teeming with fish, a market teeming with people). Note the fixed preposition "with".

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

One day we saw Kala Nag. The monsoons had burst with all their fury, and it had rained in the night. The earth, which had lain parched and dry under the withering heat of the summer sun, was teaming _____1_____ life. In little pools, frogs croaked. The muddy ground was littered with ____2___ worms, centipedes and velvety lady-birds. Grass ____3____ begun to show and the banana leaves glistened bright and glossy green. The _____4___ had flooded Kala Nag's hole. He sat in an open patch on the lawn. His shiny black hood glistened in the sunlight. He was big, almost six feet in _____5____ and rounded and fleshy, as my wrist. "Looks like a King Cobra. Let's get him."

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. crawling.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Crawling" (moving slowly on the ground) correctly describes worms and centipedes — the ground was littered with crawling worms, centipedes and lady-birds. (रेंगने वाले)

◦ Correct: The muddy ground was littered with crawling worms, centipedes and velvety lady-birds.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "singing", 3 "reading" and 4 "talking" cannot describe worms and centipedes.

NOTE

• "Crawl" = to move slowly on hands and knees or (of insects/worms) along the ground. Worms and centipedes are creatures that crawl.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

One day we saw Kala Nag. The monsoons had burst with all their fury, and it had rained in the night. The earth, which had lain parched and dry under the withering heat of the summer sun, was teaming _____1_____ life. In little pools, frogs croaked. The muddy ground was littered with ____2___ worms, centipedes and velvety lady-birds. Grass ____3____ begun to show and the banana leaves glistened bright and glossy green. The _____4___ had flooded Kala Nag's hole. He sat in an open patch on the lawn. His shiny black hood glistened in the sunlight. He was big, almost six feet in _____5____ and rounded and fleshy, as my wrist. "Looks like a King Cobra. Let's get him."

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. had.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage is narrated in the past, and the blank is followed by "begun" (past participle of "begin"). The past perfect tense "had begun" is needed. (आरंभ हो चुकी थी)

◦ Correct: Grass had begun to show ...

• Only "had + past participle (begun)" is grammatically correct; "was/is/will begun" are all wrong.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "was" would need "beginning" (was beginning); Option 4 "is" is present; Option 2 "will" is future — none fits with "begun".

NOTE

• Verb forms: begin – began – begun. The past participle "begun" must be used with "has/have/had" (had begun), not with "was/is/will".

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

One day we saw Kala Nag. The monsoons had burst with all their fury, and it had rained in the night. The earth, which had lain parched and dry under the withering heat of the summer sun, was teaming _____1_____ life. In little pools, frogs croaked. The muddy ground was littered with ____2___ worms, centipedes and velvety lady-birds. Grass ____3____ begun to show and the banana leaves glistened bright and glossy green. The _____4___ had flooded Kala Nag's hole. He sat in an open patch on the lawn. His shiny black hood glistened in the sunlight. He was big, almost six feet in _____5____ and rounded and fleshy, as my wrist. "Looks like a King Cobra. Let's get him."

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. rain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage says it had rained in the night and the monsoons had burst, so it was the "rain" that had flooded Kala Nag's hole. (वर्षा)

◦ Correct: The rain had flooded Kala Nag's hole.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "clouds", Option 3 "snow" (unlikely in monsoon) and Option 4 "heat" cannot "flood" a hole.

NOTE

• Use the context: the earlier lines mention "the monsoons had burst" and "it had rained in the night", clearly pointing to "rain" as the cause of the flooding.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

One day we saw Kala Nag. The monsoons had burst with all their fury, and it had rained in the night. The earth, which had lain parched and dry under the withering heat of the summer sun, was teaming _____1_____ life. In little pools, frogs croaked. The muddy ground was littered with ____2___ worms, centipedes and velvety lady-birds. Grass ____3____ begun to show and the banana leaves glistened bright and glossy green. The _____4___ had flooded Kala Nag's hole. He sat in an open patch on the lawn. His shiny black hood glistened in the sunlight. He was big, almost six feet in _____5____ and rounded and fleshy, as my wrist. "Looks like a King Cobra. Let's get him."

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. length.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The snake was "almost six feet in length" — "six feet in length" describes how long it was. (लंबाई में)

◦ Correct: He was big, almost six feet in length ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "six feet in weight/looks/circles" do not make sense; "feet" is a unit of length, so "in length" is correct.

NOTE

• "X units in length/height/width/depth" describes measurements: "two metres in height", "six feet in length". Here the snake's size is given in feet (a unit of length).

question: Which property of an element is inversely related to its ionisation energy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Atomic radius.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Atomic radius" is inversely related to ionisation energy. As the atomic radius increases, the outermost electron is farther from the nucleus and less tightly held, so it is easier to remove — hence the ionisation energy decreases (and vice versa). (परमाणु त्रिज्या — आयनन ऊर्जा के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Ionisation energy is the energy required to remove the outermost electron from a neutral gaseous atom.

• Across a period (left to right), atomic radius decreases and ionisation energy increases; down a group, atomic radius increases and ionisation energy decreases.

NOTE

• Ionisation energy is directly related to nuclear charge and inversely related to atomic size (radius) and shielding effect.

question: According to Census 2011 of India, what was the percentage of Christian communities of the total population in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.3%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census 2011, Christians constituted about 2.3% of India's total population. (ईसाई जनसंख्या — 2.3%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Religious composition as per Census 2011 (approx.): Hindus 79.8%, Muslims 14.2%, Christians 2.3%, Sikhs 1.7%, Buddhists 0.7%, Jains 0.4%.

• Christianity is a major religion in states like Kerala, Goa, and the North-Eastern states (Nagaland, Mizoram, Meghalaya).

NOTE

• The Census of India records data on religion, language, literacy, sex ratio, etc., and is conducted every 10 years by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.

question: In which year did the Government of India pass the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2005.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA) was passed in 2005 (and came into force in 2006). It was later renamed the "Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)" in 2009. (मनरेगा — 2005)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• MGNREGA guarantees at least 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.

• It is one of the world's largest social security/employment schemes and gives a legal "Right to Work".

NOTE

• If work is not provided within 15 days of demand, the applicant is entitled to an unemployment allowance. It is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development.

question: Find the odd one out. Vacuoles, Nucleus, Ribosomes, Lysosomes
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ribosomes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ribosomes" are the odd one out because they are NOT membrane-bound (they have no membrane), whereas the Nucleus, Vacuoles and Lysosomes are all membrane-bound organelles. (राइबोसोम — झिल्ली रहित)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis; they are made of RNA and proteins and are found free in the cytoplasm or attached to the rough ER.

• Ribosomes are the only major organelle also present in prokaryotes (bacteria), which lack membrane-bound organelles.

NOTE

• Membrane-bound organelles: nucleus, mitochondria, ER, Golgi apparatus, lysosomes, vacuoles, chloroplasts. Non-membrane-bound: ribosomes, centrioles.

question: What is the main objective of zero-based budgeting?
option_1: To assess the effectiveness of each programme and activity with the output
option_2: Establishing a relationship between inputs and outputs
option_3: Examining the objectives for which funds are provided
option_4: Re-evaluation of all the activities every year when budget provisions are made
solution_text:
The correct answer is Re-evaluation of all the activities every year when budget provisions are made.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The main objective of "Zero-Based Budgeting (ZBB)" is the re-evaluation/justification of every activity and expenditure from a "zero base" each year — nothing is carried forward automatically; every item must be justified afresh before funds are allotted. (शून्य-आधारित बजट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• In ZBB, the budget starts from a "zero base", and every department must justify all its expenses for each new period, unlike traditional budgeting which is based on the previous year's budget.

• ZBB helps in eliminating unnecessary/wasteful expenditure and ensures efficient use of resources.

NOTE

• The concept of Zero-Based Budgeting was developed by Peter Pyhrr in the USA. It was tried in Indian government departments to improve financial discipline.

question: What is the maximum amount of home loan the eligible beneficiaries can get under the 'Mo Ghara' scheme launched by the Government of Odisha in May 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Upto ₹3 lakh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the "Mo Ghara" (My House) scheme, launched by the Government of Odisha in May 2023, eligible beneficiaries can get a home loan of up to ₹3 lakh (with subsidy support) to build or improve their houses. (मो घर योजना — ओडिशा, ₹3 लाख तक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The scheme aims to help rural families construct pucca (permanent) houses and complements central housing schemes.

• "Mo Ghara" means "My House" in Odia.

NOTE

• Central housing scheme: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) — "Housing for All". States often run their own supplementary housing schemes.

question: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is taken from the USA's constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Removal of Supreme Court Judges.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The procedure for the removal (impeachment) of Supreme Court and High Court Judges was borrowed by the Indian Constitution from the USA's Constitution. (उच्चतम न्यायालय के न्यायाधीशों को हटाने की प्रक्रिया — अमेरिका से)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other features borrowed from the USA: Fundamental Rights, Judicial Review, Independence of the Judiciary, the office of Vice-President, and the preamble.

• Parliamentary Privileges and the Cabinet System were borrowed from Britain; the concept of Prerogative Writs also comes from Britain (via the USA in structure).

NOTE

• Borrowed features: USA (FRs, Judicial Review, VP, impeachment of judges); UK (parliamentary system, rule of law); Ireland (DPSP); Australia (Concurrent List).

question: The layer made up of unconsolidated rock, dust, soil, etc. that is deposited on a bed rock surface like a blanket is known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Regolith.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Regolith" is the layer of loose, unconsolidated material (rock fragments, dust, soil, etc.) that covers the solid bedrock like a blanket. (रेगोलिथ — शिथिल पदार्थ की परत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Regolith is formed by the weathering of the underlying bedrock; the soil is the uppermost, biologically active part of the regolith.

• "Talus/Scree" refers specifically to the loose rock fragments that accumulate at the base of a slope/cliff; "Protolith" is the original rock before it undergoes metamorphism.

NOTE

• The Moon's surface is also covered by a layer of regolith (fine dust and broken rock). On Earth, regolith supports plant growth once it develops into soil.

question: The famous autobiography 'Lessons life taught me unknowingly' is related to:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anupam Kher.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lessons Life Taught Me, Unknowingly" is the autobiography of the veteran Indian actor Anupam Kher. (अनुपम खेर की आत्मकथा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Anupam Kher is an acclaimed actor who has acted in hundreds of films across Indian and international cinema; he has received the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan.

• He has also served as the Chairman of the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII).

NOTE

• Autobiographies for SSC: Playing It My Way (Sachin Tendulkar), My Country My Life (L. K. Advani), On My Terms (Sharad Pawar), A Century Is Not Enough (Sourav Ganguly).

question: In December 2022, the Parliament passed the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill, 2022. This bill aims to make use of __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is non-fossil fuels.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill, 2022 (passed in December 2022) aims to promote the use of non-fossil fuels/sources (such as green hydrogen, biomass and ethanol) and to establish carbon markets to reduce carbon emissions. (गैर-जीवाश्म ईंधन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Bill amends the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, and empowers the government to specify a minimum share of non-fossil energy for certain consumers (industry, transport, buildings).

• It supports India's climate commitments made at COP-26 (Glasgow, 2021) to reach net-zero emissions by 2070.

NOTE

• Non-fossil/renewable energy sources: solar, wind, hydro, biomass, green hydrogen. Fossil fuels: coal, petroleum, natural gas (non-renewable, cause pollution).

question: Which of the following places in India receive the highest rainfall?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mawsynram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mawsynram", located in the East Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, receives the highest rainfall in India (and is often cited as the wettest place on Earth). (मौसिनराम — सर्वाधिक वर्षा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The extremely heavy rainfall is caused by the moisture-laden monsoon winds being forced up the Khasi Hills, where they cool and produce very heavy orographic rainfall.

• Cherrapunji (Sohra), also in Meghalaya, is another of the wettest places and holds several rainfall records.

NOTE

• Rainfall types: orographic (mountain-caused, as in Meghalaya and the Western Ghats), convectional and cyclonic. Meghalaya means "the abode of clouds".

question: Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma is credited with single-handedly popularising which musical instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Santoor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma is credited with single-handedly popularising the "Santoor" as a classical instrument in Hindustani music, elevating it from a folk instrument of Kashmir to the concert stage. (संतूर — पंडित शिवकुमार शर्मा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Santoor is a stringed instrument (a hammered dulcimer) played by striking the strings with a pair of light wooden mallets; it originated in the Kashmir valley.

• Shiv Kumar Sharma was awarded the Padma Vibhushan; he also composed music (as part of the "Shiv-Hari" duo with flautist Hariprasad Chaurasia) for several Hindi films.

NOTE

• Instrument–artist pairs: Santoor (Shivkumar Sharma), Sitar (Ravi Shankar), Sarod (Amjad Ali Khan), Flute (Hariprasad Chaurasia), Shehnai (Bismillah Khan).

question:
Match the army officers of the Mauryan empire in column A with the respective salaries given to them in column B.

Column A (Army Officer): a. Senapati  b. Adhvakshas  c. Mukhvas  d. Nayka   |   Column B (Salaries): i. 12,000 Pana per annum  ii. 8,000 Pana per annum  iii. 4,000 Pana per annum  iv. 48,000 Pana per annum
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Arthashastra salary structure of the Mauryan army officers, the correct matching is:

◦ a. Senapati (Commander-in-Chief) → iv. 48,000 Pana per annum (the highest-ranking officer).

◦ b. Adhvakshas → iii. 4,000 Pana per annum.

◦ c. Mukhvas → ii. 8,000 Pana per annum.

◦ d. Nayka → i. 12,000 Pana per annum.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3 (a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i).

Additional Information

• The Mauryan Empire (321–185 BCE) had a highly organised and salaried administration and a large standing army.

• Kautilya's (Chanakya's) Arthashastra is a key source describing Mauryan administration, economy and military organisation.

NOTE

• The Mauryan Empire was founded by Chandragupta Maurya (with the help of Chanakya); Ashoka was its greatest ruler. "Pana" was a silver coin used as currency.

question: In a Parliamentary system, who among the following is known as the head of the Government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prime Minister.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In a parliamentary system of government (like India's), the Prime Minister is the real executive / head of the Government, while the President is the nominal/constitutional head of the State. (प्रधानमंत्री — सरकार का प्रमुख)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The President (Head of State) is the nominal executive; the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers (Head of Government) exercise the real executive power.

• The PM is appointed by the President and is usually the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha (Article 75).

NOTE

• At the State level, the Governor is the nominal head and the Chief Minister is the real head of the government. This is the essence of the parliamentary (Westminster) system.

question: In the year 1946, a three-tiered confederation for transfer of power to India was proposed by the __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cabinet Mission.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 1946, the Cabinet Mission proposed a plan for the transfer of power to India that envisaged a three-tiered (federal) structure — a Union at the top, groups of provinces, and individual provinces at the bottom. (कैबिनेट मिशन — 1946)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Cabinet Mission (1946) consisted of three British cabinet members: Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A. V. Alexander.

• It rejected the demand for a separate Pakistan but proposed a loose federation with grouping of provinces; it also provided for the formation of a Constituent Assembly.

NOTE

• The Constituent Assembly was formed as per the Cabinet Mission Plan; its first meeting was held on 9 December 1946, with Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha as the temporary chairman.

question: In which of the following states is the Alpasi Festival celebrated annually, where a holy bath of the deities in the sea is the primary attraction?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Alpasi (Aleppey/Arattu) Festival" is celebrated annually in Kerala, where the holy bath (Arattu) of the temple deities in the sea is the main attraction. (आलपसी महोत्सव — केरल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Such temple festivals in Kerala often involve grand processions, caparisoned elephants, traditional music (chenda melam) and the ceremonial immersion/bath of the deity.

• Other famous festivals of Kerala: Onam (harvest festival), Thrissur Pooram and Vishu.

NOTE

• Kerala, "God's Own Country", is known for its temples, backwaters, Ayurveda, and classical arts like Kathakali and Mohiniyattam.

question: India played its first test match cricket against which of the following countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is England.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India played its first-ever Test match against England, at Lord's, London, in 1932. It was captained by C. K. Nayudu. (भारत का पहला टेस्ट मैच — इंग्लैंड के विरुद्ध, 1932)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India became the sixth country to be granted Test status.

• India won its first Test match in 1952 (against England at Chennai/Madras), under captain Vijay Hazare.

NOTE

• India's first Test captain was C. K. Nayudu; the BCCI's Under-23 domestic tournament is named the C. K. Nayudu Trophy in his honour.

question:
Which of the following statements is INCORRECT related to Macaulay?

A) He considered Indian and Arab literature inferior to the Western literature.  B) Macaulay was an orientalist scholar.  C) He believed that India is an uncivilised country which needs to be taught the lessons of civilisation.  D) He strongly advocated giving English language education to Indians.
option_1: He considered Indian and Arab literature inferior to the Western literature.
option_3: He believed that India is an uncivilised country which needs to be taught the lessons of civilisation.
option_4: He strongly advocated giving English language education to Indians.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Macaulay was an orientalist scholar (this statement is INCORRECT).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement B is incorrect: Macaulay was NOT an orientalist scholar — he was an "Anglicist", who strongly opposed the Orientalists and championed Western (English) education in India. (मैकाले — प्राच्यविद् नहीं, आंग्लवादी थे)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The other statements are true: Macaulay considered Indian/Arabic literature inferior to Western literature, viewed India as needing "civilising", and strongly advocated English education (in his famous "Minute on Education, 1835").

• Macaulay's Minute led to the adoption of English as the medium of higher education in India.

NOTE

• The Orientalist–Anglicist controversy was over whether to promote traditional Indian learning (Sanskrit/Arabic — Orientalists) or Western learning in English (Anglicists). The Anglicists, led by Macaulay, prevailed.

question: When was the National Digital Communications Policy launched in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2018.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "National Digital Communications Policy (NDCP)" was launched in India in 2018. It replaced the earlier National Telecom Policy of 2012. (राष्ट्रीय डिजिटल संचार नीति — 2018)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The NDCP 2018 aimed at goals such as "Broadband for All", creating jobs, attracting investment in the digital communications sector, and ensuring digital sovereignty.

• It was built around three missions: Connect India, Propel India and Secure India.

NOTE

• Related digital initiatives: Digital India (2015), BharatNet (rural broadband), and the rollout of 5G services in India (2022).

question: Pellagra is a deficiency disease that usually occurs due to lack of which of the following nutrients?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Niacin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Pellagra" is a deficiency disease caused by the lack of Niacin (Vitamin B3 / nicotinic acid) (and sometimes the amino acid tryptophan). (पेलाग्रा — नियासिन/विटामिन B3 की कमी)

• It is characterised by the "three Ds": Dermatitis, Diarrhoea and Dementia.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Niacin (Vitamin B3) is important for energy metabolism and healthy skin, nerves and the digestive system.

• Sources of Niacin: meat, fish, groundnuts, whole grains and pulses.

NOTE

• Vitamin deficiency diseases: Vitamin A – night blindness; Vitamin B1 – beriberi; Vitamin B3 (Niacin) – pellagra; Vitamin C – scurvy; Vitamin D – rickets; Vitamin K – poor blood clotting.

question: What monumental site in India houses Magan Niwas, Hriday Kunj and Vinoba-Mira Kutir?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sabarmati Ashram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sabarmati Ashram (in Ahmedabad, Gujarat) houses structures such as "Magan Niwas, Hriday Kunj and Vinoba-Mira Kutir". Hriday Kunj was Mahatma Gandhi's own residence in the ashram. (साबरमती आश्रम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Sabarmati Ashram (also called Gandhi Ashram/Harijan Ashram) was established by Mahatma Gandhi in 1917, on the banks of the Sabarmati river.

• It was from here that Gandhi began the historic Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha) in 1930.

NOTE

• "Hriday Kunj" was Gandhiji's cottage; the ashram was a centre of many activities during the freedom struggle and remains a national monument and museum.

question: The duration of bouts in each round of the International Boxing Association (AIBA Open Boxing) match for Elite and Youth Men's and Women's Competitions should be __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3 minutes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In International Boxing Association (AIBA) Open Boxing matches for Elite and Youth Men's and Women's competitions, each round lasts 3 minutes (with a 1-minute rest between rounds). (प्रत्येक राउंड — 3 मिनट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A typical elite bout consists of 3 rounds of 3 minutes each.

• Boxing is scored by judges based on the number of clean, effective punches landed.

NOTE

• India's boxing icons: Mary Kom (six-time World Champion, Olympic bronze 2012), Vijender Singh (Olympic bronze 2008), Lovlina Borgohain (Olympic bronze 2020).

question: Who is a famous Kuchipudi Dancer to receive Padma Shri in 2001?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sobha Naidu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sobha Naidu was a famous Kuchipudi dancer from Andhra Pradesh who received the Padma Shri in 2001 for her contribution to the classical dance form. (सोभा नायडू — कुचिपुड़ी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sobha Naidu was a leading disciple of the great Kuchipudi guru Vempati Chinna Satyam and was renowned for her expressive portrayals (e.g., as Satyabhama, Devi and Padmavati).

• Kuchipudi is the classical dance of Andhra Pradesh, traditionally a dance-drama form.

NOTE

• Kuchipudi is famous for the Tarangam, in which the dancer performs on the rim of a brass plate, often balancing a pot of water on the head.

question: Who among the following rulers introduced the 'jharokha darshan' in the Mughal dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Akbar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mughal emperor Akbar introduced the practice of "Jharokha Darshan" — appearing daily before the public at a balcony/window (jharokha) of the palace so that the people could see him and present their petitions. (झरोखा दर्शन — अकबर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Jharokha Darshan was meant to show that the emperor was accessible to his subjects and to reinforce the idea of the king's divine, benevolent authority.

• The practice was abolished by Aurangzeb (who considered it un-Islamic).

NOTE

• Akbar introduced several innovative practices/policies: the Mansabdari system, Din-i-Ilahi, Sulh-i-Kul (universal tolerance) and the abolition of the Jizya tax.

question: Pakhu Itu dance is performed by the Apatani tribe of which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arunachal Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Pakhu Itu" dance is performed by the Apatani tribe of Arunachal Pradesh. (अपातानी जनजाति — अरुणाचल प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Apatani tribe lives mainly in the Ziro valley of Arunachal Pradesh and is known for its unique culture, sustainable agriculture and the Ziro Music Festival region.

• A famous festival of the Apatanis is "Myoko".

NOTE

• Arunachal Pradesh, the "Land of the Dawn-lit Mountains", is India's easternmost state and home to many tribes (Nyishi, Adi, Apatani, Monpa), each with distinct dances and festivals.
